issues.display_title: Issue #583: Read the support role from /v1/auth/me, not from the JWT payload
issues.main_description_html:
Design: #578. Backend: GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#121. Follows #582.

Description

The design branch adds decodeJwtRole(token) to src/auth.ts and uses it as the primary source of the global role:

role: decodeJwtRole(token) ?? me?.role ?? null

The backend deliberately does not put the role in the JWT (Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#121): the session token has a 30-day TTL, so an embedded role would keep revoked support access alive for up to 30 days. decodeJwtRole will therefore always return null, and on the Google sign-in path — where there is no me fallback at all — user.role ends up permanently null. Result: hasSupportAccess() is always false and /support is unreachable for everyone.

Second defect in the same diff, on the session.update() refresh path:

token.role = token.role ?? data.data?.user?.role ?? null

?? keeps the first non-nullish value forever. Once a role is cached in the token it never changes, so removing someone's support role does not take effect until they sign out.

Fix direction

Drop decodeJwtRole entirely. Take role from the GET /v1/auth/me response on both the credentials and Google paths, and overwrite it unconditionally on the update trigger so a demotion actually lands.

Acceptance Criteria

  • decodeJwtRole removed from src/auth.ts
  • Credentials sign-in sets role from the /v1/auth/me payload
  • Google sign-in resolves role from /v1/auth/me too (currently has no source at all)
  • session.update() overwrites token.role with the fresh value — assignment, not ??
  • Missing or absent role in the response resolves to null, and hasSupportAccess returns false for it
  • Test: role promotion appears after session.update(); role removal also appears after session.update()
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Dependencies

#582 (port). Backend Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#121 must ship role in GET /v1/auth/me before this is verifiable end to end.

issues.display_title: Issue #584: Align support feedback list request with the backend contract
issues.main_description_html:
Design: #578. Backend: GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#124 (list/detail) and #136 (pagination). Follows #582.

Description

listSupportFeedback in src/actions/support.ts (ported in #582) does not match the endpoint the backend shipped.

1. Wrong path. It calls GET /v1/feedback. The backend moved the support list to GET /v1/support/feedback so that every support route sits behind one guard and /v1/feedback stays POST-only for regular users. Verified against the running API: GET /v1/feedback returns 405 Method Not Allowed.

2. Invalid default sort. initialFeedbackFilters.sort is updated_desc, and the value is forwarded verbatim as ?sort=updated_desc. The backend validates sort against newest | oldest | recently_updated | status and returns 400 for anything else — so the support dashboard fails on its very first load, before the user touches a control.

3. project_id filter never sent. The backend supports filtering by project, but SupportFeedbackFilters has no project_id field and the query builder never sets it.

4. Pagination is not sent or read. Added by backend #136, merged as PR #139. GET /v1/support/feedback now accepts page and per_page (defaults 1 and 20, per_page capped at 100, anything invalid → 400), and the response gained total, page, and per_page alongside feedback:

{"data": {"feedback": [...], "total": 137, "page": 1, "per_page": 20}}

listSupportFeedback sends neither parameter and reads only body.feedback, so the dashboard silently shows the first 20 rows with no way to reach the rest and no count to build a pager from.

Note: feedbackMatchesFilters and sortFeedback in src/lib/support/feedback.ts re-run filtering and sorting client-side over the server response. That was harmless while the response was the whole table; with pagination it is actively wrong, because it would re-sort a single page in isolation and reorder rows that the server already placed correctly across page boundaries. Drop them from the list path or confine them to a client-only view.

Acceptance Criteria

  • listSupportFeedback calls GET /v1/support/feedback
  • updated_desc is sent as recently_updated (rename the filter value or map it at the request boundary — do not send updated_desc)
  • Remaining sort values pass through unchanged: newest, oldest, status
  • project_id added to SupportFeedbackFilters and forwarded as a query param when set
  • page and per_page sent, and the return type carries total, page, per_page through to the caller instead of only SupportFeedback[]
  • Dashboard pager driven by the server's total, not by the length of the current page
  • Client-side sortFeedback no longer reorders the paged list (server order is authoritative across pages)
  • Test: default filters produce a request the backend accepts — correct path, and sort within the allowed set
  • Test: each filter appears in the query string only when it is not all/empty
  • Test: total from the response drives the pager, and requesting page 2 sends page=2
  • Verified against the real endpoint once the backend is deployed
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Dependencies

#582 (port). Backend Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#124 and #136 for end-to-end verification.

issues.display_title: Issue #585: Replace the Lift/Stairs area types with a draggable Access point object
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Today "Access" is not an object — it is a grouping layer over areas. An AreaLayer whose type is lift or stairs and which carries an accessId is a member of a connected Access group (PRD #513), and the group's floor span drives multi-level routing.

That makes a lift a polygon: to create one you draw an area and retype it, to move one you drag its vertices, and every cross-floor copy has to have its geometry refitted into the target floor's frame.

Access becomes its own point object instead — placed, selected and dragged exactly like a Point or Safety annotation, while keeping the cross-floor connection behaviour it has today. lift and stairs leave the area type picker entirely.

Scope

Data model

  • AreaType drops "lift" | "stairs" → "room" | "hallway" | "open-to-below".
  • New AccessPoint extends CreatedAt { id, x, y, accessId, type: "lift" | "stairs", name?, infoId?, accessOriginLevelId? } on LevelData.accessPoints — same shape family as SafetyAnnotation, plus the group fields.
  • accessId / availableLevelIds stay readable on AreaLayer for the load migration only.

Description

Scope

  6. Linked Information — section title + count chip + Unlink All as red text (not a bordered button). Rows: per-kind glyph (square for Area, pin for Point — same glyph vocabulary as the object list), Area — Room 14 type line over the linked record's name, optional 2-line description, then the eye / pencil / unlink actions. Rows separated by hairlines.
  7. Toast — "meja tester" linked to 1 object. with a green check, bottom-center, replacing the current inline lastLinked text.

issues.display_title: Issue #595: Duplicate project from the dashboard: owner-only Duplicate action wired to the new backend endpoint
issues.main_description_html:
Description

There is no way to branch off an existing project from the dashboard — the only path to a variant of a venue is rebuilding the floor plan from scratch. Add a Duplicate action that forks a project into a fully independent copy, so a user can try changes or keep a snapshot without touching the published original.

The backend does the actual copying: POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate (Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#131, merged) copies the project row, every project_files row and every stored blob, and re-points the file paths baked into the stored JSON. This task is the frontend surface for it.

Scope

Server action — duplicateProject(id) in src/actions/projects.ts: POST {API}/v1/projects/{id}/duplicate, projectActionFailure on non-OK so a 403 surfaces the owner's email like the other owner-only actions, revalidatePath("/dashboard"), returns the new Project.

Dashboard menu — a Duplicate entry in the shared ActionsMenu in src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx, rendered for both ProjectTile and ProjectRow. It runs straight from the menu with no confirmation dialog: duplicating is additive, nothing is destroyed.

Owner gating — the entry goes through the existing useOwnerOnlyGuard, so a collaborator gets OwnerOnlyDialog instead of a request, exactly like publish/unpublish/delete (§A9). OwnerOnlyAction gains "duplicate" and the dialog copy is updated to name duplicating alongside the other three.

Dashboard state — handleDuplicate in src/app/dashboard/useDashboard.ts: no optimistic row (the copy's id, project_key and thumbnail are all server-minted), set actionError on failure, then refreshList() + refreshCounts() — the copy arrives as a draft, which shifts the status tab counts.

Acceptance Criteria

  • "Duplicate" appears in the "…" menu on both the Recent tiles and the All-projects rows
  • Duplicating an owned project creates a copy named "{name} - copy" that appears in the list after the refresh
  • The copy is a draft even when the original is published, and it does not carry the original's public link
  • Editing the copy in the editor never changes the original — floor images, canvas, information records and categories are all independent
  • A collaborator (non-owner) sees the entry but gets the owner-only dialog and no request is sent
  • A backend 403 surfaces the owner-naming error in the dashboard error banner
  • Status tab counts update after a duplicate

Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#131 — POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate. Merged to development; must be deployed before this ships or the menu item 404s.

RESULT

  • src/actions/projects.ts — duplicateProject(id): POST {API}/v1/projects/{id}/duplicate, projectActionFailure on non-OK so a 403 carries the owner's email, revalidatePath("/dashboard"), returns the new Project.
  • src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx — Duplicate entry in the shared ActionsMenu, threaded to ProjectTile and ProjectRow through the existing Handlers type.
  • src/lib/collaboration/ownerGuard.ts — OwnerOnlyAction gains "duplicate".

  • No optimistic row: the copy's id, project_key and thumbnail are all server-minted and it lands as a draft, which shifts the status tab counts, so the list and counts are reconciled after the call instead of guessed.
  • The copy being a draft on its own share key is enforced by the backend, not here — the original's public link is never touched.

The building-scoping rule already exists and is used in eight places: levelsInBuilding(levels, buildings, selectedBuildingId) in src/lib/editor/levels.ts:114. It already implements the implicit-default-building fallback the PRD asks for in R2 (a level with no buildingId belongs to the first building record; a project with no buildings keeps every level in scope). issues.display_title: Issue #601: Map building floors to virtual-tour floors in Apply Based on Location
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Apply Based on Location matches a tour's floors to project floors purely by order, silently, with no way to see or change the result. groupPanosByLevel() pairs tour floor 0 with the first floor, 1 with the second, and so on. When the tour's floor order does not match the building's, panoramas land on the wrong floor and the user only finds out after the import.

Give the pairing a UI: show which building is being imported into, and let each building floor pick its virtual-tour floor.

Depends on the building-scoping task, which makes the modal the single source of routing (panoId → levelId handed to onImported). This task turns that routing from order-derived into user-chosen and renders the controls.

Scope

src/components/editor/add-panorama/ApplyLocationModal.tsx and its level-tab area.

Context header

  • Active building name, plain language: Importing into: Main Building
  • Summary line: 3 building floors, 3 virtual-tour floors detected
  • No raw ids anywhere in the UI (R16)

Mapping controls

  • One dropdown per active-building floor, each selecting one virtual-tour floor
  • Option labels use pano counts: Virtual tour floor 2 - 14 panoramas. Tour-provided floor names are not available yet — the parser drops them (see Notes), so fallback labels only for now
  • Default selection is by order, matching today's behavior: first building floor ↔ first virtual-tour floor, and so on until one list runs out. Extras stay unmapped
  • A virtual-tour floor chosen for one building floor is disabled in the others, labeled Already selected
  • Each dropdown carries a — Skip — option so a mapping can be cleared, which frees that virtual-tour floor for another dropdown
  • Helper copy: Each virtual-tour floor can be used once.
  • Warning when any virtual-tour floor is unmapped: Unmapped virtual-tour floors will not be imported. — informational, never blocking

Apply

  • Imports only panoramas whose virtual-tour floor is mapped; unmapped floors are skipped and are not dumped onto the active level as a fallback
  • Works as long as at least one floor is mapped
  • The existing per-level alignment (own dots, own links, own transform, backdrop swap) follows the mapping — retargeting a dropdown moves that group of dots to the newly selected floor
  • Existing alignment controls, per-pin drag, link lines and label toggles are unchanged

Single-floor tours (R14)

Hide the mapping block entirely when the tour has one floor or fewer — a one-row dropdown is friction with no decision behind it. The context header still shows.

Empty states

  • No virtual-tour floors detected
  • No floors in the active building

Out of scope

Remembering a mapping between imports, auto-detecting the building from the tour, and any geometry/AI floor matching — all Non-Goals in the PRD.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A single-floor tour shows no mapping controls and imports as before
  • Both empty states render
  • No raw ids in any label, option, or helper text
  • Keyboard reaches every dropdown; each has a visible label
  • Unit tests: default order mapping, duplicate prevention, clearing frees the option, unmapped floors skipped on Apply, single-floor passthrough
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Notes

Tour-provided floor names DO exist — multiple_map_data[].title, a localized object — but parseOverlay drops them (src/lib/tourmkr/overlay.ts:147), so nothing reaches the UI yet. Surfacing them is #602. This task ships the fallback labels (Virtual tour floor N - 14 panoramas); #602 swaps in the real names behind the same label helper.

Apply Based on Location now shows the active building, the floor counts on both sides, and one dropdown per building floor. Default mapping stays the old order-based pairing, so a tour that already lined up behaves identically — it is just visible and editable now. One-to-one is enforced by moving a taken floor rather than refusing the click, with the option disabled elsewhere as "Already selected". — Skip — clears a row; skipped tour floors are not imported and never fall back to the active level. Apply disables only when nothing is mapped. Single-floor tours show no controls; a building with no floors gets an empty state.

Also fixed along the way: skipping the floor you were aligning used to leave the backdrop on a floor with no dots, because the selected level key was trusted after its group disappeared. It is now read back off the surviving groups.

issues.display_title: Issue #602: Surface virtual-tour floor names from the overlay
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

The PRD in #597 asks the virtual-tour floor dropdowns to use the tour's own floor names when it has them. It does — parseOverlay just throws them away.

For a multi-floor Floor Map tour, each widgets.map.multiple_map_data[] entry carries a localized title alongside its dots. The parser reads only dots and image (src/lib/tourmkr/overlay.ts:147), so no name ever reaches ParsedOverlay, DetectedTour, or the UI. The mapping dropdowns fall back to Virtual tour floor N for every tour, even one whose floors are named.

Confirmed against a live tour — tourmkr.com/F1nDp6sEYY/47632194, two floors:

multiple_map: true
multiple_map_data[0] = { title: {"en": "1"}, image: "...", map_angle: 0, dots: 25 }
multiple_map_data[1] = { title: {"en": "2"}, image: "...", map_angle: 0, dots: 6 }

title has the same localized shape as a dot's name, so the existing nameEn() helper in the same file reads it with no new parsing code.

Scope

  • ParsedOverlay gains the per-level names, in level-index order — index i is the same index stampLevel writes onto each record, so the dropdown labels and the pano routing stay in step.
  • parseOverlay's multiple_map_data branch fills them with nameEn(lvl.title). Single-map and Journey tours produce none.
  • Carry them through toDetectedTour onto DetectedTour, next to panoramas and links.
  • The mapping dropdown uses the name when the tour has one, keeping the Virtual tour floor N fallback when it does not and the - N panoramas count either way.

Note on the observed data: the sample tour's titles are literally "1" and "2", so a name-only label renders as 1 - 25 panoramas — thin on its own. Worth deciding during implementation whether to render the name alone or keep the positional prefix (Virtual tour floor 1 - 25 panoramas) when the title is short or purely numeric. Either is a copy decision, not a data one.

Out of scope

map_angle and the per-level image are also dropped today. Neither is needed for floor mapping — leave them.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A multi-floor tour's floor names reach DetectedTour, in level-index order matching pano.level
  • Dropdown options show the tour's floor name when present, with the pano count
  • A tour with no floor names still shows Virtual tour floor N - N panoramas
  • Single-map and Journey tours are unaffected
  • A level whose title is missing or non-English-keyed degrades to the fallback label, not to an empty option

issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Overview already exists in preview/live, but only as a side effect of zooming. useAutoOutdoor (src/lib/map/useOutdoorMode.ts:41) flips a component-local boolean when the camera crosses OUTDOOR_ENTER_ZOOM / OUTDOOR_EXIT_ZOOM, and PreviewOverlay hides indoor UI while it is true. There is no way for a viewer to choose it, and no way to read which mode they are in: PreviewControls (src/components/editor/preview/PreviewControls.tsx:91) hides BuildingSelector and FloorSelector entirely while outdoor, so the one control that could show the mode disappears exactly when it matters.

The result is a viewer who zoomed out and cannot get back to a named building without hunting for it with the camera.

Scope

  • BuildingSelector (src/components/editor/BuildingSelector.tsx) gains an Overview entry above the building list, in preview/live only. The editor sidebar/map usage of this component must not change.
  • Selecting Overview activates overview mode. Selecting a building exits overview and shows that building indoors — the dropdown is the mode indicator (R5).
  • The manual choice and the zoom threshold drive one state, not two. Zooming out past the threshold selects Overview in the dropdown; zooming back into a building selects that building (that transition already resolves the building via buildingIdAtLngLat). Manual selection must survive until the user's own zoom crosses a threshold — keep the existing hysteresis, do not add a second one.
  • Selecting a building from Overview moves the camera into it (reuse getBuildingLngLatBounds + the existing BUILDING_VIEW_PITCH / BUILDING_VIEW_BEARING fit), otherwise the zoom watcher immediately re-selects Overview.
  • Keep the dropdown visible while Overview is active. FloorSelector stays hidden there (R8), and floor controls stay scoped to the selected building (R26).
  • Overview must remain usable with a single building (R12) — today BuildingSelector returns null when buildings.length === 0 and disables itself at length 1; a project with one building still needs the Overview choice.
  • View-only. No add/rename/delete/placement affordance may appear (R6, R11).

Out of scope

Context shells, shell click-to-enter, cross-building directions, and the recenter button — separate tasks against the same PRD.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Preview and live building dropdowns list Overview alongside the buildings
  • Selecting Overview switches to overview mode; floors and indoor-only UI hide
  • Selecting a building exits Overview, shows that building indoors, and moves the camera to it
  • The dropdown reads Overview after a manual zoom-out crosses the threshold, and reads the building after zooming back in
  • The dropdown stays visible and correct in overview mode
  • A single-building project can still enter Overview
  • No building management control is reachable from preview or live
  • Unit tests: the mode-resolution rule (manual pick vs zoom threshold) and the dropdown option list
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green

Refs

The design decision worth recording: the zoom watcher remains the single owner of the mode. A dropdown pick moves the camera into the zoom range that means the picked mode (zoomForMode) rather than adding a second source of truth that the next zoom event would contradict. getBuildingLngLatBounds therefore learned an optional building id, so entering a building frames that building rather than the site.

Trade-off this accepts: picking Overview always lands at zoom ≤ 16.0. On a campus that is the site view the PRD wants; on a project whose buildings are tens of metres across it reads as zoomed further out than strictly needed.

issues.display_title: Issue #608: Preview/live: keep other buildings as labeled context shells, clickable to enter
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Inside a building, the rest of the project vanishes. levelsAtOrBelow (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:266) correctly scopes indoor geometry to the active building's stack (#566), and the outdoor massing layer is all-or-nothing — useOutdoorLayer (src/lib/map/useOutdoorMode.ts:91) toggles visibility on every shell at once, tied to visible: outdoor. So the moment a viewer enters a building, every other building disappears instead of staying as site context.

The shells themselves are also inert: buildingIdAtLngLat is called only from the zoom transition (useOutdoorMode.ts:65). Clicking a building in overview does nothing.

Scope

  • Shell rendering takes a set of building ids instead of one boolean. Overview renders every building as a shell; indoor mode renders every building except the ones being shown indoors. The indoor set is the selected building plus, later, route/hover buildings — model it as a set now so #609 can add ids without another rewrite.
  • The shell label gains a building icon next to the name (R13). outdoorGeoJson already emits an outdoor-label feature per building (geojson-utils.ts:879) and OUTDOOR_LAYER_SPECS renders ["get","name"] (layer-definitions.ts:323).
  • A building with no name falls back to the project's building-name pattern rather than dropping its label — today the label feature is skipped entirely when building?.name is falsy (R19).
  • Clicking a shell selects that building and enters it indoors: set the selected building, set its active floor, move the camera. Reuse buildingIdAtLngLat or a maplibre queryRenderedFeatures hit on the shell layer — the shell carries buildingId in its properties already. Click beats hover: a click commits the selection.
  • Keep labels compact — they must not take over the map on a dense site.

Out of scope

Overview as a dropdown option, cross-building directions, hover/focus temporary indoor preview, recenter.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The selected building renders indoors; no other building shows indoor detail
  • Overview still renders every building as a shell
  • Clicking a shell selects that building, activates a floor in it, and moves the camera in

  • A building with no name still gets a label

Description

Preview and live have no recenter control. A viewer who pans or zooms away has no way back to the whole project — the only fit-all is the one-shot fitBounds on mount (PreviewOverlay.tsx:375, guarded by didFit). The editor's recenter lives in EditorCanvasZoom.tsx and operates on the 2D canvas, not the map.

The bounds helper already exists and is per-building-placement aware: getBuildingLngLatBounds (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts, #571).

Fitting a multi-building site zooms out past OUTDOOR_ENTER_ZOOM (16.25), and useAutoOutdoor watches the raw zoom event — so a naive fitBounds flips an indoor viewer into Overview, exactly what R51 forbids. The camera move must be excluded from the auto-overview rule (a suppression flag around the programmatic move, cleared when it ends). Watch moveend, not a timer: an interrupted or replaced animation must not leave the flag stuck on.

Overview dropdown, context shells, cross-building directions. Changing the auto-overview thresholds themselves.

issues.display_title: Issue #620: Import & Apply Location writes panoramas before you agree, and Cancel does not take them back
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Pressing Import & Apply Location commits every panorama the tour has no position for immediately, before the alignment step is even on screen:

// src/components/editor/add-panorama/AddPanoramaModal.tsx
function importApplyLocation() {
  const plain = pending.filter((p) => !hasLocation(p));
  const located = pending.filter(hasLocation);
  if (plain.length) commit(plain, false);   // ← writes now
  if (located.length) setAligning(located);  // ← modal opens after
}

Cancel in the alignment modal only closes it (onCancel={() => setAligning(null)}). The panoramas already written stay in the project, and the 2-second autosave persists them. A user who opened the step to look at the floor mapping and then backed out is left with markers they never agreed to import — with no undo entry they can reach after a reload.

Found while scripting a demo recording: three passes through that step left three orphaned panorama points in a real project, which had to be deleted by hand.

Why it matters beyond tidiness

Import is the one destructive-ish action in this flow, and the modal's own footer says "Line up the imported tour map with your map, then apply" — the copy promises that Apply is the commit point. The behaviour contradicts it.

Scope

  • Hold the unlocated panoramas instead of committing them. They ride along until the alignment step applies, then get committed with the aligned ones (they have no position, so the existing scatter places them — unchanged).
  • Cancel writes nothing. Closing the alignment modal by any route leaves the project exactly as it was.
  • When a tour has only unlocated panoramas there is nothing to align: keep today's behaviour — commit and close, no empty modal.
  • No copy changes, no new controls.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Opening Import & Apply Location writes nothing to the project
  • Cancel (or closing the modal) leaves the object count unchanged
  • Apply imports the aligned panoramas and the tour's unlocated ones, on the mapped floors
  • A tour whose panoramas are all unlocated still imports directly, with no alignment modal
  • Plain Import is untouched
  • Unit test covering commit-on-apply and no-commit-on-cancel

Refs

The unlocated panoramas are held in the modal and committed together with the aligned ones on Apply. Cancelling writes nothing. They still carry no position, so the importer scatters them on their routed floor exactly as before.

One AC was written wrong and is closed differently: "a tour whose panoramas are all unlocated still imports directly" cannot happen — the footer already disables the action for such a tour and says why ("This tour carries no location data."). Description

The alignment step is supposed to let the user line the tour's panorama dots up with their floor plan. On a real project it opens on a view where the floor plan is a speck:

// ApplyLocationModal.tsx
// "Centre the backdrop on the project's own location and match the editor

Note From Developer

Fixed in #654 (development cb6ce8a) → main 8ae66b9.

Root cause. Saving posts the whole canvasData through a Server Action, and Next caps that body at 1 MB by default. The 36-floor export attached here converts to ~1.66 MB of levels, so every save — toolbar button and 2-second autosave alike — returned 500 Body exceeded 1 MB limit (E394). The Go API already accepted 50 MB; the frontend was the only ceiling.

Fix. serverActions.bodySizeLimit: "16mb" plus proxyClientMaxBodySize: "20mb". The second one matters: proxy.ts matches every route, so Next clones each request body for it, and past that cap (10 MB by default) the body is truncated, not rejected — the handler then dies on half a payload with Unterminated string in JSON. The two caps are deliberately unequal so the action rejects first and says so by name. Verified against a production build: 15 MB → 200, 17 MB → 500 Body exceeded 16mb limit.

Checklist item — automatic floor mapping / same height default to false on import: done. Auto-naming was on by default and nothing turned it off for imported floors, so all 36 were renamed to Floor N the moment a floor modal mounted. Every import path now pins both toggles off, and projects imported before this heal on load rather than needing a re-import.

Worth knowing, not fixed here:

  • Autosave sends canvasData twice per cycle (updateProject then saveFloorplanAction, both writing the same canvas_data column) — 3493 KB where 1755 KB would do.
  • DB_DRIVER defaults to mysql in src/config/database.go, where gorm:"type:text" is 64 KB. Only the deployed env var keeps production on Postgres.
  • The production edge (client_max_body_size) has not been checked against a >1 MB save. Worth one POST after deploy before closing.

Design: #578. Backend: GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#136 (PR #139). Follows #582.

Description

The support list endpoint no longer returns reply history. Backend #136 removed Preload("Replies") from GET /v1/support/feedback so the list stops fetching every reply for every row, and the YAML for that endpoint now states: "Full reply history is available from the detail endpoint." GET /v1/support/feedback/:id still returns replies in full.

The ported dashboard does not survive that change, because it treats a list row as if it were a detail row.

src/app/support/SupportDashboardClient.tsx:104-105 derives both the detail and the reply dialogs from the list array rather than fetching the record:

const detailFeedback = feedback.find((item) => item.id === detailId) ?? null
const replyFeedback  = feedback.find((item) => item.id === replyId)  ?? null

SupportFeedback.replies is typed SupportReply[] (src/lib/support/feedback.ts:26) — non-optional and non-nullable — but a list row now carries replies: null. Two call sites dereference it directly:

  • SupportDashboardClient.tsx:363 — detailFeedback.replies.length → TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length'), so the detail dialog throws the moment it opens
  • SupportDashboardClient.tsx:181 — [...replyFeedback.replies, result.data] → TypeError: replies is not iterable, so sending a reply throws after the email has already been sent

getSupportFeedback(id) already exists in src/actions/support.ts:87 and calls the correct endpoint, but nothing in the client ever invokes it.

This is a frontend defect, not a backend one: the backend change is the behaviour #136 asked for, and re-adding the preload would restore the N+1 the issue was filed to remove.

  • Opening the detail dialog fetches the record via getSupportFeedback(id) instead of reading it out of the list array
  • The reply dialog uses the same fetched record, so replies is always an array
  • Loading and error states while the detail request is in flight — the dialog must not render against a half-populated record
  • After a successful reply, the dialog reflects the new reply without a full list refetch
  • SupportFeedback.replies typing matches reality: either the list and detail responses get distinct types, or replies becomes optional and every read guards it

issues.main_description_html:
Both mechanisms are meant to be dev-only conveniences. Neither is, and both ship to production.

Developer mode

src/proxy.ts:24-28 turns devModeActive on when either the x-developer-mode request header matches DEVELOPER_MODE_CODE or the dev_mode=1 cookie is present. That flag then skips the whole access-control block: the signed-out redirect (:34), protected paths (:40), the emailVerified gate (:53) and the support-role check (:61).

The cookie is set without httpOnly (:90), is unsigned, and is never verified. Measured on a local dev server with no session at all:

/dashboard  no cookie          → 307 /login
/dashboard  Cookie: dev_mode=1 → 200      ← route guard skipped

Blast radius is limited — every data path still needs a session token server-side, so the page renders empty, and proxy.ts:91-92 deletes the forged cookie on the way out, which is why /dev still 404s under a forged cookie. The header path is the unlimited one: anyone holding DEVELOPER_MODE_CODE reaches /start and /editor with an unverified or absent session, because neither page carries its own auth() check.

src/actions/dev.ts is gated on the same cookie and does nothing less than decrypt an arbitrary NextAuth JWE with NEXTAUTH_SECRET.

DISABLE_AUTH

src/lib/devAuth.ts gates on NODE_ENV !== "production", so the flag itself is inert in a deployed build. The local stand-in routes it was written for are not gated by anything:

POST /api/project   (no auth check anywhere in the file)
  → 200 {"id":"27047cf9-…","name":"unauthenticated write test","status":"draft"}
  → wrote /tmp/gothru-3d-floormap/projects/27047cf9-….json

src/app/api/project/route.ts, src/app/api/project/[id]/route.ts and src/app/api/live/[key]/route.ts compile into every build and check nothing. An unauthenticated caller can make the server create a directory and write attacker-named JSON files, one per request.

The bypass also no longer does what it advertises — /api/files stopped serving the local /tmp copies, /api/predict forwards upstream regardless, saveFloorplanAction has no local branch, and getToken() returning "" sends Bearer on 12 call sites. It is strictly worse than not setting the flag.

Scope

Delete both. Files removed: src/lib/devAuth.ts, src/actions/dev.ts, src/app/dev/page.tsx, src/components/dev/SessionTokenDecoder.tsx, src/app/api/project/route.ts, src/app/api/project/[id]/route.ts, src/app/api/live/[key]/route.ts, plus their tests. Edited: src/proxy.ts, src/actions/projects.ts, src/lib/server/session.ts, src/app/api/upload/route.ts, src/app/api/predict/route.ts, src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx, src/components/editor/preview/useDirectionMapLayers.ts, .env.example.

The nav-grid debug overlay ("round dots" on preview) goes with it — it is the only cosmetic thing developer mode unlocked.

issues.display_title: Issue #662: Integrate design/wizard-mappedin into development: preserve imported buildings on Add More Floors + per-building floor ordering
issues.main_description_html:
Frontend integration task for #650 (PRD) / #657 (design + spec). Design work is finished on design/wizard-mappedin; this issue carries it onto development.

PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-11-wizard-mappedin-add-more-floors-building-safety/prd.md (branch product-docs)
Design branch: design/wizard-mappedin
Spec issue: #657 · PRD issue: #650 · Related: #643

Problem

Mappedin imports can contain several buildings. The review modal groups them, but the grouping dies one step later: when the user picks Add More Floors instead of Continue to Editor, imported floors are flattened into one project-wide list. Reordering then looks harmless but can silently move a floor into the wrong building, and a manually uploaded image floor has no clear home.

Heads-up: design/mappedin-import-building-grouping (#643) never landed on development

#643 is closed as completed, but its helpers exist only on design/mappedin-import-building-grouping:

  • src/lib/mappedin-import/groupBuildings.ts — absent from origin/development
  • src/lib/mappedin-import/mergeIntoProject.ts — absent from origin/development
  • src/components/setup/import-mappedin/BuildingGroupSection.tsx — absent from origin/development

design/wizard-mappedin carries both #643 and the new wizard work, so this integration covers #643 as well — no separate integrate issue needed. Nothing needs to be written from scratch; mergeImportIntoProject and groupFloorsByBuilding are already pure and tested on the branch.

Scope

  1. Add More Floors — imported buildings and per-floor building membership survive the jump into the upload step.
  2. Manual/image floors — default to Main Building, shown as a normal building group once it has floors.
  3. Floor ordering step — grouped by building for multi-building projects; reorder within a group only.
  4. Continue to Editor — the editor opens with exactly the structure the wizard showed.

Requirements

Same table as #657 (R1–R16). Musts in short: preserve imported buildings (R1) and per-floor membership (R2); manual floors → Main Building (R3, R4); grouped ordering (R5, R6) that never changes membership (R7); readable names with Building N / Main Building fallbacks (R8, R9); editor handoff preserves structure and order (R11); removals stay scoped to one building (R12, R13); single-building imports stay lightweight (R14); image-only flow unchanged (R15); no raw ids or file internals in the UI (R16).

Where membership is lost today (verified on origin/development)

  1. src/lib/mappedin/parse.ts:64 — floorStacks.flatMap((stack) => stack.floors ?? []). A Mappedin floor stack is a building; every stack collapses into one flat floorIds list. Nothing downstream can recover it.
  2. src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:358-370 — the returned canvasData is {levels, coordSpace, mapRotationDeg, mapOffsetX/Y}: never sets buildings, never stamps buildingId.
  3. src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx:186-189 (Add More Floors) — raw level prepend, no Building record created, no buildingId stamped; paired with addImportedFloorsToWizard (runImport.ts:59). Every imported floor from every batch lands in the one implicit default building.
  4. Siblings on the same data — fixing only #3 leaves these flattening: StepUploadFloor.tsx:135 (Continue to Editor replaces canvasData wholesale), StepGenerate.tsx:90 (createBlankCanvasData on the step-4 exit), src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts:169-175 (force-stamps every imported level with selectedBuildingId), src/hooks/useDigitalTwinExport.ts:62 (twin rebuild keeps {levels, coordSpace} only).

Data shape: FloorConfig (src/store/useMapStore.types.ts:24-32) has no building field. Membership is LevelData.buildingId? (:276) plus CanvasData.buildings? (:303), so it rides save/undo/publish for free. levelsInBuilding (src/lib/editor/levels.ts:117-128) resolves unstamped levels to buildings[0] — everything downstream already reads through it, so no downstream changes are needed once levels are stamped. Imported floors are local component state only (StepUploadFloor.tsx:53) and are not persisted by src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts.

Files (from design/wizard-mappedin, 39 files / ~2.3k insertions incl. PRD docs)

Port as-is (new, pure, already tested): src/lib/mappedin-import/{groupBuildings,mergeIntoProject}.ts, src/lib/wizard/floorBuildings.ts, src/components/setup/import-mappedin/BuildingGroupSection.tsx, src/components/setup/step-list-floor/{BuildingFloorGroup,FloorStack}.tsx, src/components/setup/step-upload/UploadedGroup.tsx, src/components/setup/step-list-floor/useFloorReorder.ts, plus their __tests__.

Re-apply call sites by hand on current development: src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx, src/components/setup/StepListFloor.tsx, src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx, src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts, src/components/editor/AddLevelModal.tsx, src/lib/mappedin/{parse,types}.ts, src/lib/mappedin-import/{detectSource,extractFloors,runImport}.ts, src/lib/editor/levels.ts (fillMissingLevels), src/store/mapStore/floorsSlice.ts, src/components/setup/import-mappedin/{FloorListSection,ImportSummaryModal,ImportModalActions,types}.

Call shape: mergeImportIntoProject({ groups: groupFloorsByBuilding(importResult), levels: src.canvasData.levels, canvasData, floorConfigs, keepIds: true[, prepend: true] }) → setCanvasData / setFloorConfigs / selectBuilding(staged.buildingId) / setActiveLevelId(staged.levelId).

Merge hazards

  • The branch forked at c8a9806; development is 11 commits ahead, and both StepUploadFloor.tsx and useAddLevel.ts changed in that window.
  • keepImportedFloorSettings() (from the #626 autosave fix) exists nowhere on design/wizard-mappedin. The existing calls at StepUploadFloor.tsx:141 and useAddLevel.ts:197 on development must survive the port — do not take the branch's component versions wholesale.
  • mergeIntoProject.ts:65-70 guard: a project with levels but zero Building records has them in the implicit default; appending an imported building would make the import buildings[0] and silently adopt them. The helper materializes a real "Untitled building" record and stamps existing levels first — keep that behavior and its test.

Tests

  • Multi-building import stays grouped after Add More Floors.
  • Imported floors keep their original building membership.
  • A manual/image floor added after import lands in Main Building.
  • Step 3 reorder changes order only within one building.
  • Cross-building reorder does not change membership.
  • Removing an imported floor does not disturb other buildings.
  • Removing a manual floor does not disturb imported buildings.
  • Continue to Editor preserves imported buildings, Main Building, and floor order.
  • Regression: single-building import stays simple.
  • Regression: image-only wizard flow unchanged.
  • Keep the ported groupBuildings / mergeIntoProject / levels / floorBuildings / useFloorReorder suites green.

Acceptance checklist

  • Add More Floors preserves imported Mappedin buildings.
  • Add More Floors preserves imported floor membership.
  • Manual/image floors added after import go to Main Building.
  • Main Building is visible when manual floors exist in a multi-building project.
  • Floor ordering is grouped by building for multi-building projects.
  • Reorder works within a building group and never moves floors between buildings.
  • Continue to Editor preserves imported buildings, Main Building, and floor order within each building.
  • Removing floors does not disturb unrelated buildings.
  • Single-building imports remain simple; image-only wizard flows remain unchanged.
  • Copy is clear, plain, and non-technical.
  • tsc --noEmit, eslint, and vitest pass.

Manual verification

  1. New project → import a Mappedin file with at least two buildings → Add More Floors.
  2. Add one image floor manually, continue to the floor ordering step.
  3. Confirm imported floors are grouped under their imported buildings and the manual floor sits under Main Building.
  4. Reorder floors inside one imported building — the floor stays in that building.
  5. Continue to the editor and confirm the same building + floor structure.
  6. Repeat with a single-building import, then with an image-only flow (no Mappedin) — both unchanged.

Out of scope

Moving floors between buildings in the wizard · a full building manager in the wizard · renaming buildings or imported floor names in the review modal · guessing which imported building a manual floor belongs to · billing, permissions, collaboration, publishing, viewer, embed · new import formats.

RESULT

Branch: feature/662-integrate-design-wizard-mappedin · Commit: a99b08f · 38 files, +1717/-326

design/wizard-mappedin ported onto development file by file (git merge is off-limits in this repo). 32 files were taken as-is; three were hand-merged because development had moved too: StepUploadFloor.tsx, useAddLevel.ts, floorsSlice.ts — the only delta against the design branch in those three is development's keepImportedFloorSettings (#626), restored at all four call sites. This also carries #643, which was closed but never reached development.

What changed

  • Both wizard exits — Continue to Editor and Add More Floors — stage the reviewed groups through mergeImportIntoProject: each imported building becomes its own Building record and every level is stamped with its own buildingId, never the selected one (R1/R2).
  • Manual/image floors go to Main Building (R3/R4); step 2 shows it as a group only once an import has put other buildings on screen, so the image-only flow is untouched (R14/R15).
  • Step 3 orders floors inside a building group; reorderWithinBuildings keeps each building's slots, so a drag across a boundary reorders within the floor's own building instead of moving it (R5/R6/R7).
  • fillMissingLevels replaces createBlankCanvasData on the step-4 exit, so generating no longer discards staged buildings and geometry (R11).
  • Removing a floor drops its level with its config, and an emptied group stops rendering rather than lingering (R12/R13).

Two defects found while porting, both fixed

useDigitalTwinExport.openInEditor deleted the structure the wizard had just built. It rebuilt canvasData as {levels, coordSpace}, dropping canvasData.buildings and every buildingId, and rebuilt floorConfigs from dt.levels alone. An imported Mappedin floor has serverPath: "", so it never scans, never enters the twin — and was deleted by "Open Editor" after Generate, undoing the preservation work rebuildTwin had done thirty lines earlier. Now mergeTwinIntoCanvas (pure, extracted, tested) lays each scanned level over the one already stored, keeps the floors the twin does not carry, spreads the rest of canvasData, and orders levels by floorConfigs.

Main Building was identified by name. fillMissingLevels picked the manual bucket with b.name === "Main Building". A Mappedin floor stack can legitimately be named that, and the import then absorbed every uploaded image floor while the UI still labelled those floors "floor plans you added here" — R4 failing silently. Building.imported now marks import-created records, and the bucket is found by that flag in fillMissingLevels, groupFloorConfigsByBuilding and BuildingFloorGroup.

Both were found by an adversarial review pass over the staged diff: 19 candidate findings, 17 refuted against the code, these 2 confirmed.

Checks

tsc --noEmit pass · eslint pass · vitest 137 files, 1085 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed (was 1080 — 5 new regression tests in levels.test.ts and useDigitalTwinExport.test.ts, on top of the ported groupBuildings, mergeIntoProject and floorBuildings suites).

issues.display_title: Issue #664: Editor Map: other buildings as clickable outer shells, no Overview state (PRD #591 R1-R22)
issues.main_description_html:
In Editor Map mode a multi-building project shows one building at a time. The others only appear when the user zooms far enough out for useAutoOutdoor to flip the whole map to massing (src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx:107), and that view is edit-disabled — so the creator either sees indoor detail with no site context, or site context they cannot touch.

PRD #591 R1-R22 removes that trade-off: the selected building always stays indoors, every other building renders as a named outer shell alongside it, and clicking a shell switches to that building. Editor Map mode gets no Overview state and never shows every building as a shell.

The machinery already exists — preview grew it in #608/#609. outdoorGeoJson takes a buildingIds filter (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:915) and useOutdoorLayer already accepts shellBuildingIds + onSelectBuilding (src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx:404). This task points the editor at the same layer instead of the zoom watcher. Preview and live behaviour must not change (R8).

Design branch design/editor-map-outer-buildings carries a version of this against a 69-commit-old base; it renders shells via setFilter/excludeBuildingId and bakes canvas label chips. Reuse the current shellBuildingIds path rather than reintroducing the old one.

Scope

  • src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts — remove outdoorMode / setOutdoorMode (only the two editor toolbars read it; preview keeps its own local state)
  • src/components/editor/EditorBottomToolbar.tsx, MapTransformControl.tsx — drop the outdoor-disabled branches
  • src/lib/map/useBuildingDrag.ts — a press on a shell selects the building instead of starting a drag (R22)

  • Clicking a shell selects that building; the building selector and active floor follow (R15-R19)
  • Clicking empty map space, or the already-selected building, changes nothing (R20, R21)
  • In move mode, a click on another building's shell selects only — the same gesture does not drag it (R22)
  • Preview and live outdoor behaviour unchanged (R8)

RESULT

Editor Map no longer has a zoom threshold. useAutoOutdoor is gone from Editor3DMapView, and with it the outdoorMode store flag the bottom toolbar and the transform popup used to refuse to edit in — there is no state to refuse in any more (R5/R6). The selected building stays indoors and every other building is a permanent context shell.

The shell layer is the one preview grew in #608 — shellBuildingIds plus select-on-click — so preview and live behaviour are untouched (R8). The list comes from outerBuildingIds, which is viewerBuildingSplit with Overview, routes and hover preview all off: sharing the rule means the editor can never shell the building it is editing (R21). Empty on a single-building project, so nothing is drawn.

In move mode a press on a shell selects only (R22): hitsGuardLayer bails before the drag disables dragPan, and the shell layer's own click handler switches buildings. Hovering a shell now restores the cursor it replaced instead of clearing it, which used to leave move mode looking disarmed.

Bug found while recording the demo, fixed here (d0f91b4): no outer building has ever shown its name — not in Editor Map, and not in the preview Overview that shipped the shells in #608. The label feature was built as a LineString whose two vertices are the same coordinate, and geojson-vt simplifies a zero-length line out of existence, so it never reached a tile. querySourceFeatures on the outdoor source said it plainly: 41 shell features, zero labels. It is a Point now; queryRenderedFeatures on the label layer returns "Community Centre Demo" and it is on screen in the demo (R11). The fix lands in preview too.
